from: The Buddha awakened under a tree next to a river. There’s something about practicing outdoors — with the ground underfoot, the sounds of wind and water, and the steadiness of the natural world — that opens a different quality of attention.
to: Practice outdoors with the ground underfoot and the sounds of wind and water. Walking and meditating together gives us time to notice our surroundings and how we meet them.

from: Kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity aren’t just nice ideas
to: Kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity (steadiness through change) aren’t just nice ideas

from: No registration is necessary for this class, and it is open to all community members.
to: No program registration is needed. To join on Zoom, create a member account and sign in; the session link is on My Home.

from: Whether you are new to these practices or have been practicing for many years, you are welcome to join us as we learn and practice together.
We hope you will join us and discover the benefits of cultivating greater warmth, openness and care in your life and our shared world.
